title: Should Emergency Physicians and Nurses Direct Their Patients to YouTube for Heparin Self-Injection Training? A Systematic Review of Social Media Videos
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of 161 unique English-language YouTube videos on low-molecular-weight-heparin (LMWH) self-injection. It reports quantitative shares of items with an explicit denominator: 67/161 (41.6%) classified as 'Misleading Information' and 10/161 (6.2%) containing information that may harm the patient. INCLUDED, but the headline 41.6% figure is a COMPLETENESS criterion (Total Comprehensiveness Score < 6), not a truth judgement, so it is coded construct=QUALITY per the governing rule; the harm/incorrect-technique share is coded CONTENT.

estimates.country: not stated for the videos (all English-language YouTube videos; authors based in Istanbul, Turkey)
estimates.measure_type: % of YouTube LMWH self-injection videos categorised as containing 'Misleading Information' (Total Comprehensiveness Score < 6)
estimates.denominator: 161 unique eligible English-language YouTube videos on LMWH self-injection (458 retrieved by 5 keyword searches; 185 excluded as irrelevant/no audio/non-English/no visual; multipart and duplicate videos condensed)
estimates.definition: Videos scoring 6/6 on the Total Comprehensiveness Score (all six injection steps demonstrated) from both physician raters were 'Useful Information'; every other video, including accurate videos that omitted a step, was categorised 'Misleading Information'
estimates.misinfo_def: "Misleading Information: Videos that were judged by the reviewers here to contain misleading information included inaccurate information or videos that did not contain any information on LMWH injection administration. In addition, videos that had only relatively useful information or contained any relatively misleading information were categorized as misleading. (eg, not all steps were covered or wrong technique)."
estimates.source_quote: (58.4%) were categorized as useful, and 67 (41.6%) of them were categorized as misleading.
estimates.page_loc: Results, p. 384 (also Abstract; Table 2 n = 67 vs n = 94)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two independent emergency physicians, blinded to each other's scores, trained by a professor of emergency medicine against Memorial Sloan Kettering and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS patient-education references; disagreements decided by that professor. Inter-rater agreement kappa = 0.987; ICCs 0.86-0.98 for the M-DISCERN/GQS/TCS/JAMAS scores (all P < .001).
estimates.moderator_quote: Videos included in the Useful Information group were those that received a TCS of 6 when evaluated by 2 separate emergency medicine physicians. In contrast, videos that received a TCS score < 6 by one or both of the evaluating physicians were considered to be in the Misleading Information group.
estimates.notes: CONSTRUCT CALL FOR THE ADJUDICATOR: the paper calls this group 'Misleading Information', but membership is decided by a 6-item completeness checklist (TCS < 6), so a wholly accurate video that omits one step is counted as 'misleading'. That is exactly the case the instructions assign to QUALITY ('If a wholly true item could receive the label ("misleading" = covers < 4 screener items), it is QUALITY'). Row kept, must be excluded from prevalence. breadth left blank per the QUALITY rule. denom_selection is blank because the authors took ALL search results (458), not a top-N slice: 'In our study, all LMWH injection videos on YouTube were evaluated, yet other studies included a certain number of the most-watched videos'. Videos are not country-attributed; only English-language videos were eligible.

estimates.country: not stated for the videos (all English-language YouTube videos; authors based in Istanbul, Turkey)
estimates.measure_type: % of YouTube LMWH self-injection videos containing information that may harm the person receiving the injection (wrong site, wrong angle, breach of sterility)
estimates.value_raw: 10 (6.2%) of them contained information that may harm the person getting the injection
estimates.denominator: 161 unique eligible English-language YouTube videos on LMWH self-injection
estimates.definition: Video demonstrated content that could harm the patient: noncompliance with sterility rules, injection into the wrong area, or injection at the wrong angle (i.e. technique contradicting the reference guidelines). All 10 were in the Misleading Information group.
estimates.misinfo_def: "10 (6.2%) of them contained information that may harm the person getting the injection (noncompliance with sterility rules, injection to the wrong area, and at the wrong angle)."

estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same two emergency physicians, coding against the Memorial Sloan Kettering / Cambridge University Hospitals injection-procedure references; kappa = 0.987 for the reliability assessment of videos.
estimates.moderator_quote: According to this training, a 6-step algorithm (Total Comprehensiveness Score [TCS]) of self-injection has been adapted (Figure 1). Two independent emergency physicians evaluated included videos separately.
estimates.notes: This is the stricter, genuinely truth-anchored numerator in the same country x platform cell as the QUALITY row: content that actively contradicts injection guidelines (wrong site/angle, non-sterile technique), not merely incomplete. Hence construct=CONTENT, definition_variant=true, borderline=true (an adjudicator could read 'may harm' as a safety rather than a veracity label). The same 10 videos are also reported as 14.9% of the 67 misleading videos ('our study found that 10 videos (14.9%) of the misleading group could put one's health at risk'); the within-misinformation version is NOT extracted separately because the all-videos denominator (6.2%) is the poolable one.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) The 14.9% version of the harm figure (10/67 within the misleading group) was not given its own row - it is the same numerator on a misinformation-only denominator, and the 6.2%/161 form is already extracted. (2) Source-composition shares (individuals/patients 49.1% of creators; 95.5% of misleading videos created by individuals/patients; university/professional channels 50.0% of useful videos) describe WHO produced the videos, not the prevalence of misinformation, so no rows. (3) M-DISCERN, GQS, JAMAS and TCS are reported as medians per group (Tables 2-3), i.e. scale scores with no share of items above a threshold, so per the instructions no additional QUALITY rows. (4) '4 (2.4%) of the videos included in the study had recommendations to prevent postinjection complications' is a share of accurate/helpful content, not misinformation. (5) Comparison figures for other studies (Ozsaban 80.8%, Culha 88.1%, Chang and Park 76%) are cited from elsewhere and are excluded by R8. (6) The videos have no country attribution; country_norm=Global may need review if the review's convention is to attribute the search locale (Turkey).

rob.design: Systematic content analysis of YouTube; frame = all 458 videos returned by 5 drug-name keyword searches on 20 August 2021, 161 unique videos after excluding non-English (62), irrelevant topic (83), no audio (31), no visual (9) and after collapsing duplicates/multipart videos; two independent emergency physicians rated every video blinded to each other with a third (professor) adjudicating; Cohen's kappa = 0.987, ICC 0.86-0.98, P < .001; protocol not preregistered; reviewers were both physicians rather than an interdisciplinary team.
rob.item6_quote: Misleading Information: Videos that were judged by the reviewers here to contain misleading information included inaccurate information or videos that did not contain any information on LMWH injection administration. In addition, videos that had only relatively useful information or contained any relatively misleading information were categorized as misleading. (eg, not all steps were covered or wrong technique).
rob.item10_quote: Of these videos, 94 (58.4%) were categorized as useful, and 67 (41.6%) of them were categorized as misleading.
